questions.question: Growing of two or more crops simultaneously on the same field is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mixed cropping**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mixed cropping** is an agricultural practice where **two or more crops** are grown **simultaneously** on the **same piece of land**.
 
• The primary objective of this method is to **minimize the risk** of total crop failure. If one crop fails due to **adverse weather conditions**, **lack of rainfall**, or **pest infestation**, the other crop ensures some insurance against complete loss.
 
• In mixed cropping, the seeds of the different crops are typically **mixed together** and sown in the field without any **definite row arrangement** or specific spatial pattern.
 
• Farmers generally choose crop combinations that have **different nutrient requirements** or different **root depths** to ensure that they do not compete intensely for the same resources.
 
• Common examples of mixed cropping in **India** include combinations such as **Wheat + Gram**, **Wheat + Mustard**, or **Groundnut + Sunflower**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inter-cropping**:
 
 
• Similar to mixed cropping, it involves growing two or more crops simultaneously, but in a **definite row pattern**.
 
• For example, a few rows of one crop may alternate with a few rows of another crop (e.g., **Soybean + Maize**).
 
• This method allows for **better management** of fertilizers and pesticides for individual crops compared to mixed cropping.
 
 
 
• **Mono-cropping**:
 
 
• This refers to the practice of growing only **one type of crop** on the same piece of land **year after year**.
 
• While it allows for **specialization** and **mechanization**, it often leads to the **depletion of specific soil nutrients** and increases the risk of **pest outbreaks**.
 
 
 
• **Crop Rotation**:
 
 
• It is the practice of growing different types of crops in the **same area** in **sequential seasons**.
 
• For instance, planting a **leguminous crop** (like pulses) after a **cereal crop** (like wheat) helps in **nitrogen fixation** and replenishes **soil fertility** naturally.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Diverse Cropping Systems**:
 
 
• These systems improve **soil health**, increase **biodiversity**, and provide a **varied diet** and **income source** for farmers.
 
• They are essential components of **sustainable agriculture** and help in **weed control** and efficient **utilization of solar energy**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The Work-Energy theorem states that the total work done on an object is equal to:

options.text: Change in the work and energy of the body
Change in the potential energy of the body
Change in the kinetic energy of the body
Change in the static energy of the body

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Change in the kinetic energy of the body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Work-Energy Theorem** states that the **net work done** by the sum of all forces acting on an object is equal to the **change in the kinetic energy** of that object.
 
• This principle is derived from **Newton's Second Law of Motion** and is applicable to both **constant** and **variable forces**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Mathematically, the theorem can be expressed as **W = ΔK**, where **W** is the **total work done** and **ΔK** is the **change in kinetic energy** (Final KE - Initial KE).
 
• The formula for **Kinetic Energy (KE)** is **1/2 mv²**, where **m** represents the **mass** of the body and **v** represents its **velocity**.
 
• If the **net work** done on an object is **positive**, its **kinetic energy increases**, meaning the object speeds up. If the **net work** is **negative**, the **kinetic energy decreases**, and the object slows down.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Work Done:**
 
 
• In **physics**, **work** is done when a **force** acts upon an object to cause a **displacement**. It is a **scalar quantity**.
 
• The **SI unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**, which is equivalent to **1 Newton-meter (N·m)**.
 
• The formula for work is **W = Fd cosθ**, where **F** is force, **d** is displacement, and **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.
 
 
 
• **Potential Energy (PE):**
 
 
• **Potential Energy** is the energy held by an object because of its **position** relative to other objects, stresses within itself, or its **electric charge**.
 
• The most common form is **Gravitational Potential Energy**, calculated as **PE = mgh**, where **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity** (approximately **9.8 m/s²** on Earth) and **h** is the **height**.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE):**
 
 
• It is the energy that a body possesses by virtue of being in **motion**. 
 
• Since it depends on the **square of the velocity**, kinetic energy is always a **non-negative** value.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Energy:**
 
 
• This law states that **energy** can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be **transformed** from one form to another.
 
• In a **closed system** where only **conservative forces** act, the sum of **Kinetic Energy** and **Potential Energy** remains **constant**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scalar Nature:** Both **Work** and **Energy** are **scalar quantities**, meaning they have magnitude but no **direction**.
 
• **Power:** The **rate** at which **work** is done or **energy** is transferred is called **Power**. Its **SI unit** is the **Watt (W)**, where **1 Watt = 1 Joule per second**.
 
• **Static Energy:** This usually refers to **Electrostatic Energy** (energy stored in an electric field) or potential energy in a stationary state, but it is not the primary component defined by the **Work-Energy Theorem**.
 
• **Applications:** The **Work-Energy Theorem** is widely used in **engineering** and **mechanics** to solve problems where **force** and **displacement** are known, avoiding the need to calculate **acceleration** via **Newton's Second Law**.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of creating DNA copies during reproduction?

options.text: To change the structure of cells
To make organisms immune to diseases
To pass genetic information to offspring

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To pass genetic information to offspring**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)** replication is the fundamental process during **reproduction** that ensures the **genetic blueprint** is transferred from one generation to the next.
 
• In a dividing cell, the **nucleus** contains information for the inheritance of features from parents to **offspring** in the form of **DNA** molecules.
 
• The process of **DNA copying** creates two copies of the genetic material; these copies need to be separated from each other, with each going to a new daughter cell.
 
• Simply creating a **DNA copy** is not enough; it must be accompanied by the creation of an additional **cellular apparatus** (like mitochondria, ribosomes, etc.) so that the DNA copies have a functioning environment to survive. ***Hence, the primary purpose is to pass genetic information, making this statement the correct answer.***
 
• The consistency of **DNA copying** during **reproduction** is important for maintaining the **body design** features that allow an organism to use a particular niche.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of DNA:** 
 
 
• **DNA** is a double-stranded **helical structure** first described by **James Watson** and **Francis Crick** in **1953**.
 
• It is composed of **nucleotides**, which consist of a **phosphate group**, a **deoxyribose sugar**, and four types of **nitrogenous bases**: **Adenine (A)**, **Thymine (T)**, **Guanine (G)**, and **Cytosine (C)**.
 
 
 
• **The Role of Variations:**
 
 
• No biochemical process, including **DNA copying**, is **100% accurate**. Small alterations occur during the process, leading to **variations** in the offspring.
 
• These **variations** are the source of **evolution** and allow species to survive in changing environments or **ecological niches** over long periods of **time**.
 
• While drastic changes in DNA can lead to the death of a cell, subtle **variations** provide a competitive advantage in the struggle for survival.
 
 
 
• **Heredity and Genes:**
 
 
• A **gene** is a specific segment of **DNA** that provides information for making a particular **protein**.
 
• If the information in the **DNA** changes, different **proteins** will be made, eventually leading to altered **body designs** or **traits**.
 
• **Heredity** is the process by which **traits** and characteristics are transmitted from **parents** to **progeny** through these **genetic codes**.
 
 
 
• **Modes of Reproduction:**
 
 
• In **asexual reproduction**, a single parent produces **DNA copies** that are almost identical, resulting in **clones** with very little variation.
 
• In **sexual reproduction**, **DNA** from two different individuals combines, leading to a greater degree of **variation** and genetic diversity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location:** In **eukaryotic cells**, the majority of **DNA** is located in the **cell nucleus**, organized into structures called **chromosomes**. A small amount of **DNA** can also be found in **mitochondria** (mtDNA) and **chloroplasts**.
 
• **Cell Division:** Before **mitosis** or **meiosis** begins, the cell enters the **S-phase** (Synthesis phase) of the **cell cycle**, where **DNA replication** occurs.
 
• **Biological Significance:** Without **DNA copying**, the continuity of life would cease because new cells would lack the instructions necessary to perform **metabolic functions** or maintain **biological structures**.
</ul

questions.question: A car is moving at a speed of 180 km/h. After the brakes are applied, it comes to a complete stop in 5 seconds. If the total mass of the car along with its passengers is 4200 kg, what is the force applied by the brakes to stop the car?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**–42,000 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The calculation of force is based on **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, which states that **Force (F) = mass (m) × acceleration (a)**.
 
• First, we must convert the **initial velocity (u)** of the car from **km/h** to **m/s** to maintain **SI unit** consistency. Given the speed is **180 km/h**, we multiply by **5/18**. Therefore, **u = 180 × (5/18) = 50 m/s**.
 
• The car comes to a **complete stop**, which means the **final velocity (v)** is **0 m/s**. The **time (t)** taken for this change is **5 seconds**.
 
• We calculate the **acceleration (a)** using the first equation of motion: **v = u + at**. Rearranging for **a**, we get **a = (v - u) / t**. Plugging in the values: **a = (0 - 50) / 5 = -10 m/s²**. ***Hence, the acceleration is –10 m/s².***
 
• The total **mass (m)** of the system (car + passengers) is **4200 kg**. Using the force formula: **F = 4200 kg × (-10 m/s²) = -42,000 N**.
 
• The **negative sign** in the result **–42,000 N** signifies that the force is acting in the **opposite direction** to the motion of the car, which is characteristic of a **braking or retarding force**. ***Hence, the correct answer is –42,000 N.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion**: This law provides a quantitative measure of force. It establishes that the **net force** acting on an object is equal to the rate of change of its **linear momentum**. For an object with a constant mass, it simplifies to the product of **mass** and **acceleration**.
 
• **Unit Conversion**: In physics problems, it is crucial to use the **International System of Units (SI)**. Velocity should be in **meters per second (m/s)**, mass in **kilograms (kg)**, and time in **seconds (s)**. The conversion factor **5/18** is derived from **1000 meters / 3600 seconds**.
 
• **Concept of Retardation**: When the velocity of an object decreases over time, the acceleration is negative. This is specifically referred to as **retardation** or **deceleration**. In this context, the brakes provide the necessary **frictional force** to cause this retardation.
 
• **The Newton (N)**: The SI unit of force is the **Newton**, named after **Sir Isaac Newton**. **1 Newton** is defined as the amount of force required to accelerate a **1 kg** mass at a rate of **1 m/s²**.
 
• **Applications**: Understanding braking force is essential in **automotive engineering** and **road safety**. It helps in determining **stopping distances** and designing efficient **braking systems** like **ABS (Anti-lock Braking System)** to handle large **inertial loads**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Momentum**: The **initial momentum** of the car was **4200 kg × 50 m/s = 210,000 kg·m/s**. The **final momentum** is **0**. The **impulse** provided by the brakes is equal to this change in momentum.
 
• **Force Direction**: Since force is a **vector quantity**, the sign is vital. A positive force would imply the car is speeding up, while the **negative force** confirms the application of brakes to reduce speed.
 
• **Mass Sensitivity**: If the **mass** of the car were lower, the same **braking force** would stop the car in **less time** or a **shorter distance**, demonstrating the role of **inertia** in motion.

questions.question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement about the endoplasmic reticulum?

options.text: The endoplasmic reticulum helps in the transport of materials within the cell, especially between the cytoplasm and the nucleus.
The endoplasmic reticulum stores genetic material in it.
The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) has ribosomes attached to its surface, which help in protein synthesis.
The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is involved in the synthesis of lipids (fat molecules).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The endoplasmic reticulum stores genetic material in it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** serves as a channel for the **transport of materials**, especially proteins, between various regions of the **cytoplasm** or between the **cytoplasm** and the **nucleus**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Genetic material**, specifically **Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA)**, is stored within the **Nucleus** of the cell, not the **Endoplasmic Reticulum**. The ER is primarily involved in the **synthesis** and **transport** of molecules, while the nucleus acts as the control center containing hereditary information. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)** is characterized by the presence of **ribosomes** attached to its outer surface. These ribosomes are the primary sites for **protein synthesis** within the cell. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** lacks ribosomes and is responsible for the **synthesis of lipids**, including **fats**, **steroids**, and **phospholipids**. It also plays a role in **carbohydrate metabolism**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the incorrect statement (and the correct answer) is that the endoplasmic reticulum stores genetic material.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of ER:** The **Endoplasmic Reticulum** was first observed by **Keith Porter**, **Albert Claude**, and **Ernest Fullam** in **1945**. It is a large network of membrane-bound **tubules** and **sheets** called **cisternae**.
 
• **Detoxification:** One of the crucial functions of the **Smooth ER** (SER) in the **liver cells** of **vertebrates** is **detoxifying** many poisons and **drugs**, making them water-soluble so they can be excreted from the body.
 
• **Membrane Biogenesis:** Some of the proteins and lipids synthesized by the ER help in building the **cell membrane**. This biological process is known as **membrane biogenesis**.
 
• **Calcium Storage:** In **muscle cells**, a specialized type of smooth ER called the **sarcoplasmic reticulum** stores **calcium ions**, which are essential for **muscle contraction**.
 
• **Protein Folding:** The **Rough ER** (RER) provides a surface where **proteins** are folded into their **three-dimensional structures**. Proteins that are improperly folded are usually retained or degraded.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum** is absent in **prokaryotic cells** (like bacteria) and **mature mammalian red blood cells (RBCs)**.
 
• It accounts for more than **half of the total membrane** in many **eukaryotic cells**.
 
• The **lumen** of the ER is the internal space enclosed by the ER membrane, which is distinct from the surrounding **cytosol**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following examples represents motion along a straight line?

options.text: A child running around a park
A train moving on a straight track

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A train moving on a straight track**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Motion** is defined as the change in the **position** of an object with respect to **time** and its surrounding environment. Depending on the path taken by the object, motion is classified into various types.
 
• **Rectilinear Motion**: This refers to the movement of an object along a **straight line**. In this type of motion, the **direction** of the object remains constant throughout its path.
 
• **A fan blade rotating**: This represents **rotational motion** or **circular motion**. The particles of the fan blades move in a circular path around a **fixed axis**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **A child running around a park**: Since a park usually involves a curved or circular boundary, the path is not a single straight line. This is typically an example of **curvilinear motion** or **circular motion**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **A train moving on a straight track**: When a train travels on tracks that do not curve, every part of the train moves the same distance in a **straight path**. This is a classic example of **rectilinear motion**. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• **A pendulum swinging**: This is an example of **periodic motion** or **oscillatory motion**. The bob of the pendulum moves **to and fro** about a central **mean position** at regular intervals of **time**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Translatory Motion**:
 
 
• It occurs when all parts of an object move the **same distance** in the same **interval of time**.
 
• It is divided into two categories: **Rectilinear motion** (motion in a **straight line**, e.g., a **falling stone**) and **Curvilinear motion** (motion along a **curved path**, e.g., a **thrown ball**).
 
 
 
• **Circular and Rotational Motion**:
 
 
• **Circular motion** is when an object moves along the **circumference** of a circle (e.g., a **satellite** orbiting the **Earth**).
 
• **Rotational motion** occurs when an object turns around an **internal axis** (e.g., the **spinning of the Earth** or a **spinning top**).
 
 
 
• **Periodic and Oscillatory Motion**:
 
 
• **Periodic motion** repeats itself after a fixed **period of time** (e.g., **hands of a clock**).
 
• **Oscillatory motion** is a specific type of periodic motion where the object moves **back and forth** (e.g., **vibrating strings** of a **guitar** or a **child on a swing**).
 
 
 
• **Random Motion**:
 
 
• This occurs when an object moves in a **disorderly manner** with no fixed path or direction (e.g., the **motion of a honeybee** or **gas molecules**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distance vs. Displacement**: In **rectilinear motion**, if an object moves in a single direction without turning back, the magnitude of **distance** is equal to the magnitude of **displacement**.
 
• **Uniform Rectilinear Motion**: When an object covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time** along a straight line, it is said to be in **uniform motion**, meaning its **velocity** is constant.
 
• **Non-Uniform Rectilinear Motion**: If the **speed** of the object changes while moving in a straight line, it is called **accelerated motion** or non-uniform linear motion (e.g., a **car** starting from rest on a straight road).
 
• **Newton's First Law**: It states that an object will remain in its state of **rest** or **uniform motion** in a **straight line** unless acted upon by an **external unbalanced force**.
</ul

• The Moon, being much closer to Earth than the Sun, exerts a stronger **tidal force**. This force is "differential" because the gravitational attraction is stronger on the side of the Earth facing the Moon than on the center or the far side, causing the water to bulge.

questions.question: Which of the following best differentiates a mixture from a compound?

options.text: Mixtures always have a fixed boiling point.
Mixtures can be separated by physical methods, while compounds require chemical methods.
Compounds retain the individual properties of their components.
Compounds are heterogeneous in nature, while mixtures are always homogeneous.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mixtures can be separated by physical methods, while compounds require chemical methods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mixtures** consist of two or more substances that are physically combined but not chemically bonded. Because there are no chemical bonds between the components, they can be separated using **physical methods** such as **filtration**, **distillation**, **crystallization**, or **magnetization**. In contrast, **compounds** are substances formed by the chemical combination of elements in a **fixed proportion**. To separate a compound into its constituent elements, **chemical methods** or **electrochemical reactions** like **electrolysis** are required. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• A **mixture** does not have a **fixed melting or boiling point**. Instead, it typically exhibits a **range of temperatures** during phase changes because the composition can vary. Conversely, **compounds** are pure substances and possess sharp, **fixed boiling and melting points**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• In a **mixture**, each constituent substance **retains its original properties**. For example, in a mixture of **iron filings** and **sulfur**, the iron can still be attracted by a magnet. However, when a **compound** is formed (like **Iron Sulfide**), the individual properties of the elements are lost, and the new substance has entirely different **chemical and physical characteristics**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Compounds** are always **homogeneous** in nature, meaning they have a uniform composition and appearance throughout. **Mixtures** can be **homogeneous** (like **solutions**) or **heterogeneous** (like **suspensions** or **soil**), where the different components are visible to the naked eye or under a microscope. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous Mixtures**:
 
 
• **Homogeneous mixtures** have a **uniform composition** throughout their mass. Examples include **air**, **alloys** (like **brass**), and **salt dissolved in water**.
 
• **Heterogeneous mixtures** do not have a uniform composition. Examples include a **mixture of sand and sugar**, **chalk powder in water**, or **oil and water**.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Compounds**:
 
 
• Compounds follow the **Law of Definite Proportions**, which states that a chemical compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by **mass**. For example, **Water (H2O)** always contains **hydrogen** and **oxygen** in a **1:8 mass ratio**.
 
• The formation of a **compound** involves a **chemical change** accompanied by the absorption or evolution of energy in the form of **heat**, **light**, or **electricity**.
 
 
 
• **Separation Techniques**:
 
 
• **Physical methods**: Used for mixtures. **Chromatography** is used to separate colors, and **centrifugation** is used to separate **cream from milk**.
 
• **Chemical methods**: Used for compounds. **Thermal decomposition** uses heat to break down a compound into simpler substances (e.g., **Calcium Carbonate** breaking into **Calcium Oxide** and **Carbon Dioxide**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy Changes**: During the preparation of a **mixture**, **energy** (heat, light, etc.) is usually neither given out nor absorbed. However, the preparation of a **compound** is always accompanied by a significant **energy change**.
 
• **Composition**: The components of a **mixture** can be present in **any ratio**, whereas the elements in a **compound** are always present in a **fixed, definite ratio** by weight.
 
• **Purity**: **Compounds** are considered **pure substances** because they consist of only one type of molecule, while **mixtures** are considered **impure substances**.
</ul

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Particles to come closer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Applying pressure to a gas results in the reduction of the space between its constituent particles. Because gases have **large intermolecular spaces**, increasing external pressure forces these particles into a smaller total volume, which effectively makes the **particles come closer** to each other. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• According to **Boyle's Law**, at a **constant temperature**, the pressure of a given mass of an ideal gas is **inversely proportional** to its volume. This means that when pressure is increased, the **volume must decrease**, not increase. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The speed at which particles move is a function of their **kinetic energy**, which is directly proportional to the **absolute temperature** of the gas. • When a gas is compressed (pressure is increased), work is done on the system. In most real-world scenarios, such as **adiabatic compression**, this causes the **temperature to increase** rather than decrease. A decrease in temperature usually requires the gas to expand or for heat to be removed from the system. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The high **compressibility** of gases is one of their most significant physical properties, distinguishing them from **liquids and solids**, where particles are already very close together.

• **Liquefaction of Gases:** By applying **high pressure** and **reducing temperature**, gases can be converted into liquids. This is the principle used in the production of **LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas)** and **Liquid Oxygen** used in hospitals.
 
• **Compressibility Factor:** In **thermodynamics**, the deviation of a real gas from ideal gas behavior is measured by the compressibility factor (**Z**). For an ideal gas, **Z = 1**, but for real gases, this value changes depending on the pressure and temperature.
 
• **Diffusion and Effusion:** Because particles in a gas are far apart and move rapidly, they can easily mix with other gases (**diffusion**) or escape through tiny openings (**effusion**). Increasing pressure can influence the rate at which these processes occur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Industrial Applications:** Compressed gases like **CNG (Compressed Natural Gas)** are used as fuel in vehicles because large volumes of gas can be squeezed into **small cylinders** by applying high pressure.
 
• **Ideal Gas Equation:** The relationship between pressure, volume, and temperature is summarized by the equation **PV = nRT**, where **P** is pressure, **V** is volume, **n** is the number of moles, **R** is the **universal gas constant**, and **T** is the temperature.
 
• **Mean Free Path:** When pressure increases and particles come closer, the **mean free path** (the average distance a particle travels between collisions) **decreases**. This leads to an increase in the frequency of collisions against the walls of the container.
</ul

questions.question: The average age of 32 students of a class is 21 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 22 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:

Increase in Average = 22 − 21 = 1 year

**∴ The correct answer is 54 years.**

 Deviation Method Total Persons = 32 + 1 = 33 | Avg Increase = 22 − 21 = 1 Old Avg: 21 + Increase: 33 × 1 = 33 
 Teacher's Age = 21 + 33 = 54 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 32 students = 32 × 21

⇒ Total age of 32 students = 672 years

⇒ Total number of persons after including the teacher = 32 + 1 = 33

⇒ Total age of 33 persons = 33 × 22

⇒ Total age of 33 persons = 726 years

⇒ Age of the teacher = Total age of 33 persons − Total age of 32 students

⇒ Age of the teacher = 726 − 672 = 54 years

**∴ The correct answer is 54 years.**

When a new member joins a group and the overall average increases, the new member brings their share of the old average plus the extra weight distributed to everyone.

If one person is replaced by another and the average changes, the number of people remains the same.

Value of New Person = Value of Replaced Person + (Total Persons × Change in Average)

questions.question: Two trains are running along parallel tracks towards each other at speeds of 40 km/h and 60 km/h, respectively. If the length of each train is 125 metres, then how much time will they take to cross each other?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 40 + 60 = 100 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/s = 100 × (5/18) = 250/9 m/s.

Total distance covered = 125 + 125 = 250 metres.

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative speed = 250 ÷ (250/9) = 9 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Speed of Train 1 = 40 km/h

Speed of Train 2 = 60 km/h

Length of both trains = 125 m each

**Formula Used:**

Time taken to cross = (Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2) ÷ Relative Speed

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

 
 
 
• Train 1 (125m) 
• 40 km/h Train 2 (125m) 
• 60 km/h Total Distance = 125 + 125 = 250 m Relative Speed = 40 + 60 = 100 km/h 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 125 m + 125 m = 250 m

⇒ Relative Speed (moving towards each other) = 40 + 60 = 100 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 100 × (5/18) = 250/9 m/s

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 250 ÷ (250/9)

⇒ Time = (250 × 9) / 250

⇒ Time = 9 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 9 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

When two bodies travel in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Total Distance in Crossing

When a train crosses another train, bridge, or platform, the total distance covered is always the sum of the lengths of both objects (L₁ + L₂).

questions.question: Accordioning to the Indian Government how many Khelo India State Centres of Excellence (KISCEs) were notified by the Government of India as of June 2025?

• As of **June 2025**, the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** has notified a total of **34** **Khelo India State Centres of Excellence** (**KISCEs**) across **31 States and Union Territories** in **India**.
 
• The **KISCE** initiative is a flagship program under the **Khelo India Scheme**, aimed at upgrading existing sports infrastructure in **States** and **Union Territories** to a world-class standard.
 
• Each center is tasked with focusing on specific **Olympic sport disciplines** to ensure concentrated development of talent and resources, helping **India** improve its standing in the **Olympic Games**.
 
• The selection of these **34** centers is based on the quality of existing infrastructure, coaching facilities, and the performance history of the **State** in particular sports.
 
• Financial assistance is provided by the **Central Government** to these centers to cover recurring and non-recurring costs, including **sports science** support, high-performance coaches, and technical equipment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Khelo India Scheme**:
 
 
• Launched in the financial year **2017-18**, this umbrella scheme was introduced by the **Government of India** to revive the sports culture at the grassroots level.
 
• The scheme is divided into **12 verticals**, ranging from infrastructure development to talent identification and community coaching.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Objectives**:
 
 
• The primary goal of **KISCE** is to create a robust ecosystem for athletes who have moved past the introductory stage and are ready for high-performance training.

• **Role of States and UTs**:
 
 
• While the **Central Government** provides the funding and technical guidelines, the day-to-day management of these **34** centers remains with the respective **State Governments** or **UT Administrations**.
 
• This collaborative model ensures that the development of sports is not centralized but spread across the diverse geography of **India**.

questions.question: How many cities were covered under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) by June 2025 to combat air pollution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**131**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** is a long-term, time-bound, national-level strategy to tackle the air pollution problem across India in a comprehensive manner.
 
• By **June 2025**, the total number of cities covered under this flagship program is **131**.
 
• These cities are primarily identified as **non-attainment cities**, which means they did not meet the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)** for five consecutive years.
 
• The program initially started with **102 cities** in **2019**, which was later expanded to **122**, and eventually to **131** cities to include those receiving grants under the **XV Finance Commission** for million-plus population cities.
 
• The primary objective of covering these **131 cities** is to implement city-specific action plans to reduce the levels of **Particulate Matter (PM10 and PM2.5)** significantly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Launch and Governance:**
 
 
• The **NCAP** was launched in **January 2019** by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**.
 
• It represents the first such effort in **India** to frame a national framework for air quality management with a time-bound reduction target.
 
 
 
• **Revised Targets:**
 
 
• Initially, the goal was to achieve a **20% to 30% reduction** in particulate matter concentration by **2024** (with **2017** as the base year).
 
• In **September 2022**, the Government of India updated the goal to a **40% reduction** in particulate matter levels or achieving the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards** by **2025-26**.
 
 
 
• **PRANA Portal:**
 
 
• To monitor the progress of the program in these **131 cities**, the government launched **PRANA (Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities)**.
 
• This portal tracks the physical and financial status of city action plan implementation and disseminates information on air quality to the public.
 
 
 
• **Funding Mechanisms:**
 
 
• Funding for the program is funneled through the **Control of Pollution** scheme for **82 cities** with a population below one million.
 
• For the remaining **49 cities** (million-plus cities), funding is provided through the **XV Finance Commission** air quality grants.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Multi-Sectoral Approach:** The **NCAP** focuses on various sources of pollution, including **industrial emissions**, **vehicular exhaust**, **biomass burning**, and **construction dust**.
 
• **Institutional Framework:** It involves collaboration between the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)**, and **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)** to ensure ground-level execution of clean air plans.
 
• **Monitoring Stations:** As part of the program, there has been a significant increase in the number of **Manual Monitoring Stations** and **Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS)** across the **131 identified cities** to provide real-time data.
 
• **Base Year:** The base year for measuring the concentration of pollutants and calculating the percentage of reduction is **2017**.
</ul

questions.question: Which regulatory provisions did the the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) reference while imposing the fine on Acko General Insurance for violations related to outsourcing and commissions in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Section 40(1) of Insurance Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** took regulatory action against **Acko General Insurance** in **May 2025** for violations concerning **outsourcing** and **commission** payments.
 
• **Section 40(1)** of the **Insurance Act, 1938** serves as a critical provision that prohibits the payment of **remuneration** or **reward** by way of **commission** to any person for soliciting or procuring insurance business in **India**, unless that person is an authorized **insurance agent** or an **insurance intermediary**.
 
• The investigation by **IRDAI** revealed that the insurer had entered into arrangements that resulted in payments exceeding the permissible **commission caps** or were directed toward entities not eligible under the regulatory framework.
 
• The fine was imposed because the **outsourcing** expenses were found to be a means of circumventing the statutory limits on **acquisition costs** and **expenses of management**. *Hence, the statement regarding Section 40(1) is correct.*
 
• This regulatory intervention emphasizes the necessity for **general insurance companies** to adhere strictly to the **Insurance Act** and **IRDAI regulations** to maintain market integrity and protect **policyholders'** interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI):**
 
 
• It is a **statutory body** formed under the **IRDAI Act, 1999**.
 
• The **headquarters** of the authority are located in **Hyderabad**, having moved from **New Delhi** in **2001**.
 
• Its primary mission is to regulate and promote the **insurance** and **reinsurance** industries in **India** while ensuring the **financial security** of the sector.
 
 
 
• **The Insurance Act, 1938:**
 
 
• This is the **foundational legislation** governing the insurance sector in **India**.
 
• It provides the **legal framework** for the **registration** of insurance companies, **investment** of assets, and the **prohibition** of rebates and unauthorized commissions.
 
• **Section 64V** of this Act specifically deals with the **assets and liabilities** of an insurer and the determination of the **solvency margin**.
 
 
 
• **Outsourcing Regulations:**
 
 
• Under the **IRDAI (Outsourcing of Activities by Indian Insurers) Regulations, 2017**, insurers are strictly prohibited from outsourcing **core functions** such as **underwriting**, **claims settlement**, and **compliance** functions.
 
• The regulations aim to ensure that insurers retain **effective control** over their operations and do not utilize outsourcing as a loophole to pay extra **commissions**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Section 40(1) Enforcement:** The enforcement of this section ensures that the **cost of insurance** does not escalate due to unregulated **payouts** to intermediaries, which ultimately benefits the **end consumer**.
 
• **Compliance Framework:** Every insurer must submit an **annual certificate** signed by the **CEO** and **Compliance Officer**, affirming that all **outsourcing** arrangements and **commission** payments are in line with the **statutory provisions**.
 
• **Penalties:** **IRDAI** has the power to impose **monetary penalties** ranging from **1 lakh** to **1 crore** rupees per day of continuing violation or cancel the **certificate of registration** under extreme circumstances.
</ul

questions.question: In November 2025, the standing committee of the National Board for Wildlife approved a proposal to construct a Pinjoli bridge in which of the following wildlife sanctuaries?

• The **Standing Committee** of the **National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)**, in its meeting held in **November 2025**, cleared the proposal for the construction of the **Pinjoli bridge**.
